```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, cache = T, fig.width=8, fig.height=4)
options(scipen = 0, digits = 3)  # controls base R output
if(!require('pacman')) {
  install.packages('pacman')
}
pacman::p_load(ggplot2, dplyr, tidyverse, gridExtra, ggrepel, plotly, skimr, tidytext, stringr, caret, xgboost, fastDummies, here)
# install a package if it does not exist already and put the package in the path (library)
# dplyr, ggplot2,tidyr
dir.create(here("models"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

```

```{r}
#loading dataset
data_prediction <- read.csv(here("data", "processed", "weather_wide_pivot.csv"))

# 2. Remove non-numeric columns and define features and label
data_model <- data_prediction %>%
  select(-CurrentDate) %>%
  dummy_cols(remove_selected_columns = TRUE)# drop non-feature columns

X <- data_model %>% select(-Label) %>% as.matrix()
y <- data_model$Label

```

```{r}
set.seed(123)

# Split into 80% train, 20% test
train_index <- createDataPartition(y, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
X_train <- X[train_index, ]
y_train <- y[train_index]

X_test <- X[-train_index, ]
y_test <- y[-train_index]

```


1st XGBoost Model with Cross-Validation to determine best number of rounds
```{r}
# DMatrix for all data
dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_train, label = y_train)

set.seed(123)
cv_model <- xgb.cv(
  data = dtrain,
  nrounds = 150,
  nfold = 5,
  early_stopping_rounds = 10,
  maximize = TRUE,
  objective = "binary:logistic",
  eval_metric = "auc",
  verbose = 1
)

```

```{r}

# Extract performance metrics
cv_log <- cv_model$evaluation_log

# Plot
ggplot(cv_log, aes(x = iter)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = train_auc_mean, color = "Train AUC")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = test_auc_mean, color = "Validation AUC")) +
  labs(title = "AUC per Boosting Round",
       x = "Boosting Round (nrounds)",
       y = "AUC") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Train AUC" = "blue", "Validation AUC" = "red"))

```


```{r}
best_nrounds <- cv_model$best_iteration

final_model <- xgboost(
  data = dtrain,
  nrounds = best_nrounds,
  objective = "binary:logistic",
  eval_metric = "auc",
  verbose = 0
)
```

```{r}
# #Saving/loading models
```

```{r}

dtest <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_test)

# Predict probabilities
y_pred_prob <- predict(final_model, dtest)

# Convert to 0/1 labels (using threshold 0.5)
y_pred <- ifelse(y_pred_prob > 0.5, 1, 0)

# Accuracy
accuracy <- mean(y_pred == y_test)
print(paste("Test Accuracy:", round(accuracy, 4)))

```

```{r}
confusionMatrix(factor(y_pred), factor(y_test))
```

2nd XGBoost Model
```{r}

# 1. Create DMatrix
dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_train, label = y_train)
dtest <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_test, label = y_test)

# 2. Calculate scale_pos_weight to handle imbalance (optional but recommended)
# ratio = (# of negatives) / (# of positives)
neg <- sum(y_train == 0)
pos <- sum(y_train == 1)
scale_weight <- neg / pos

# 3. Set parameters to favor recall
params_recall <- list(
  booster = "gbtree",
  objective = "binary:logistic",
  eval_metric = "auc",  # You could also use 'logloss'
  scale_pos_weight = scale_weight,  # Helps model pay more attention to minority class
  max_depth = 11,
  eta = 0.075,
  gamma = 1,
  subsample = 0.7,
  colsample_bytree = 0.8,
  lambda = 1
)

# 4. Train the model
set.seed(123)
final_model_recall <- xgb.train(
  params = params_recall,
  data = dtrain,
  nrounds = 100,
  watchlist = list(train = dtrain, test = dtest),
  early_stopping_rounds = 10,
  print_every_n = 10
)

# 5. Predict with LOWER threshold to favor recall
pred_probs <- predict(final_model_recall, X_test)
threshold <- 0.4  # lower threshold to boost recall
pred_labels <- ifelse(pred_probs > threshold, 1, 0)

# 6. Evaluate
confusionMatrix(factor(pred_labels), factor(y_test), positive = "1")
```
